intent: Thin rule that separates content, horizontal or vertical, with an optional label or action on the line.
useWhen: Separating groups of content inside one surface (form groups, menu-like stacks, card bodies)
An 'or' break between two choices, e.g. between sign-in methods
A 'Show more' or 'Add' action sitting on the line between list sections
A vertical rule between items in a toolbar or metadata row
doNotUseWhen: Card or Section edges that already draw a border — let the container own it
Inside Section headers or PageHeader — they have their own structure
As a spacer — use space tokens (gap, margin) for whitespace
Between table rows or list rows — Table, DataTable, and ListView draw their own row lines
Headed groups of content — use Section or a heading

label.note: Short text on the line. Horizontal only; ignored when vertical.

align.note: Position of label and action on the line. Horizontal only.

action.note: One inline control, normally kit Button variant="tertiary" size="sm". Horizontal only.

tone.note: faint uses border.faint; default uses border.strong

requirements: Plain horizontal divider renders <hr> (implicit separator role)
Vertical divider renders role="separator" with aria-orientation="vertical"
With label or action, the line segments are aria-hidden and the label is plain text; no separator role, so the label stays readable
action keeps its own accessible name (a kit Button with visible text)

doNot: Do not invent a local Divider, Separator, or <hr> style
Do not use Divider for spacing or to add margins
Do not stack Divider against a container border
Do not put long text in label — keep it to a word or two
